Restoring the last-run-only reader rejects the honest receipt before a clean row can be returned; alternatively treating inherited as newly added prevents this clean outcome.
Returning inherited as added instead of subtracting the measured primary failures makes the independently expected empty added-ID set false.

Dropping the inherited ID or binding it to a commit other than the independently created and actually merged fixture primary changes the expected mapping; this is not merely the receipt echo, since selection comes from git history.

Always remeasuring instead of reading the cached receipt appends twice rather than once; never measuring appends zero times. The injected list element is fixture-controlled and this assertion proves call count only, not the requested revision.
